what_it_does: This paper describes the process of adapting a legacy Fortran-based plasma turbulence simulation called Gysela to run on modern graphics processing units (GPUs) from AMD. Plasma simulations model the behavior of hot ionized gas in fusion reactors and require massive computational power. The team used two different approaches: a simpler translation layer for most of the code and a complete rewrite for the performance-critical collision operator (the part computing how particles interact). The work was benchmarked on AMD's latest processors and GPU accelerators.
